title: Fixed affine additive coefficient augmentation quasi-isomorphism
statement: Let X be a separated scheme, U a finite family of opens with every positive tuple intersection affine, and I an injective resolution of X.etaleAdditiveSheaf. There is a chain map b from the ordinary unit cechOver X.toSpecGamma U complex, after forgetting module scalars and applying AddCommGrpCat.uliftFunctor, to additiveCechTotal U I. For every degree n and ordinary cochain x, b.f n (ULift.up x)=additiveCechBeta U I n x, and b is a quasi-isomorphism. No covering condition or compactness assumption is required.

proof.text: Identify the lifted ordinary unit Cech complex with the Cech complex of additive structure sections on opens. In each tuple coordinate use restrictFunctorGamma.inv; its naturality identifies the cofaces and their alternating sums. Forgetting scalars and ULift preserve the finite products. The natural tensor-unit section coordinates identify these with the usual quasi-coherent unit sheaf coefficients.

Apply I.iota.f 0 on each tuple and include in bidegree (n,0). Naturality commutes with horizontal differentials and I.iota_f_zero_comp_complex_d makes the vertical differential vanish. Thus these components define a chain map with precisely additiveCechBeta coordinates. This construction uses no injective-row augmentation theorem.

Affine quasi-coherent acyclicity, obtained from the finite affine etale Cech vanishing criterion and the tensor-unit coordinates, makes all positive derived evaluations of the additive structure sheaf vanish on each tuple intersection. Degree-zero left exactness identifies the augmentation kernel with coefficient sections. Exact products commute with these evaluations and homology, so the augmented vertical columns are quasi-isomorphisms.

Transpose the bicomplex, apply the first-quadrant column augmentation criterion, and transport through the standard sign isomorphism between the two totals. The finite diagonal filtration proves that the constructed b is a quasi-isomorphism. Degree zero uses the same kernel calculation; an empty tuple index family yields the zero complexes, even without a cover.

theorem exists_additiveCech_beta_quasiIso
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.IsSeparated] {ι : Type u} [Finite ι]
    (U : ι → X.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ (k : ℕ) (y : Fin (k + 1) → ι), IsAffineOpen (⨅ l, U (y l)))
    (I : InjectiveResolution X.etaleAdditiveSheaf) :
    ∃ b : (((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, ⊤)) AddCommGrpCat.{u} ⋙
        AddCommGrpCat.uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj
          (cechOver X.toSpecΓ U (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf))) ⟶
        additiveCechTotal U I,
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : (cechOver X.toSpecΓ U
        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).X n),
        b.f n (ULift.up x) = additiveCechBeta U I n x) ∧ QuasiIso b
